events.title: IBM System/360 announced
events.summary: IBM announced the System/360 family on April 7, 1964 — a compatible line of mainframes that shared software across models.
events.about: System/360 introduced the idea that one architecture could span small and large machines — programs written for a low-end 360 could run on a big iron box with more I/O. OS/360, COBOL batch jobs, and enterprise data processing all standardized on this family. The `/360` name even inspired later product lines (System/370, z/OS descendants).

narrative.whyChosen: System/360 defined compatible computer families and dominated business computing for decades.
narrative.whyImportant: Software compatibility across hardware tiers became an industry expectation — still how cloud instance types work today.
narrative.problemSolved: Customers faced incompatible machines every upgrade; IBM needed one architecture from lab to datacenter.
